metadata.name: Peninsular Railway (Santa Clara County interurban)
metadata.note: The Peninsular Railway - "the Pin", "Big Red" - was the Southern Pacific's electric interurban in western Santa Clara County: hourly red cars from the Market Street depot in San Jose west along Stevens Creek Road and down the SP Mayfield Cut-off through Cupertino and Los Altos to Palo Alto and Stanford, southwest via Saratoga to Los Gatos with a branch to Congress Springs, and south through Campbell to Los Gatos, plus Palo Alto's city streetcars. It grew out of the San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban Railway (opened 19 March 1904, quietly SP-controlled from April 1904), the Peninsular Railroad (incorporated 21 December 1905) and the Santa Clara Interurban (Palo Alto streetcars from 15 November 1906), all consolidated as the Peninsular Railway on 30 June 1909. Through San Jose-Palo Alto service began 5 March 1910. Routes were cut back from 1925 (Palo Alto locals), 1929 (Palo Alto/Stanford), 1932 (Campbell, Congress Springs) and 1933 (via Saratoga); the last interurban ran 30 September 1934.
metadata.ownership_note: Rule 4 judgment. (1) Southern Pacific controlled the San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban from April 1904 and owned the Peninsular throughout, but the trains ran under the San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban name until the 30 June 1909 consolidation and under the Peninsular name, timetables and livery after it, never as SP trains - so each operating company keeps its own colour and nothing is drawn in SP red (#C1272D). (2) Features are split at 30 June 1909, when the predecessors' trains became Peninsular trains. (3) The Peninsular Railroad (1905) and Peninsular Railway (1909) are treated as ONE company: the same SP-controlled corporation reincorporated under a near-identical name, with the same president. (4) The brief reserved one spare colour, #7BA05B, for Peninsular predecessors; it is given to the San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban. The Santa Clara Interurban Railroad is a different company, so it gets its own new colour #6E8B3D (checked absent from data/ before use) rather than sharing #7BA05B.
metadata.colour_note: Peninsular Railway #3A7D44; San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban Railway #7BA05B; Santa Clara Interurban Railroad #6E8B3D (new). Checked programmatically: every feature in data/ carrying each company string has the identical colour.
metadata.mode_note: Rule 7: the regional San Jose-Los Gatos, San Jose-Palo Alto, Cupertino-Los Gatos and Congress Springs routes linked separate communities and are mode "interurban" (dashed). The Palo Alto city lines and the Palo Alto depot-Stanford shuttle ran within one built-up area and are "streetcar".
metadata.sp_track_note: Where Peninsular cars ran on or beside SP property it is drawn as Peninsular service: (a) the Mayfield Cut-off (SP Los Altos Branch), Mayfield-Monta Vista-Congress Junction, where the Peninsular had its own electrified track on the SP right of way; (b) Campbell, where the Campbell route paralleled the SP Vasona line and briefly shared the SP narrow-gauge Almaden branch. The SP's own steam passenger trains on the cut-off (to 1964) and to Los Gatos are NOT drawn here - they are Southern Pacific service.
metadata.geometry_quality: No straight-line legs anywhere. All 15 features are wholly or partly street-routed on today's OSM road centrelines (Rule 2: a later alignment than the line's own era, since the roads have been widened and the interurban often ran on private right of way beside them). The Mayfield Cut-off sections (Monta Vista-El Camino Real 8.56 mi, Monta Vista-Congress Junction 4.27 mi) are traced from OpenHistoricalMap relation 2749538 (CC0), which is the SP track on the shared right of way. Campbell Avenue-Camden Avenue (about 0.9 mi) is on the OSM ex-SP Vasona Industrial Lead. Mileage checks: San Jose-Saratoga 11.18 mi vs documented 11; Saratoga-Los Gatos 4.03 mi vs documented 4. Per-feature detail is in each geometry_quality. Every finished line passed reversal (>120 deg on legs >200 m) and revisit (<350 m after >1 km of path) checks with zero hits.
metadata.omitted: Deliberately not drawn: (1) the Alum Rock line and the Berryessa Road (1913-1934) and King Road (1923-1934) routes in San Jose - Peninsular-owned, but Wikipedia says passenger service was often run by San Jose Railroads, and they are San Jose city/suburban routes left to the San Jose Railroads layer; (2) the Bascom and Naglee Park local routes in San Jose, transferred to San Jose Railroads in 1933 (city streetcars, other layer); (3) the San Jose & Santa Clara Railway, which Santa Cruz Trains says was consolidated into the Peninsular in 1909 but which ran as part of San Jose Railroads (other layer); (4) the 1909 "stub service" on the Mayfield Cut-off that Wikipedia mentions without dates or termini; (5) Peninsular freight (Congress Springs quarry, Alum Rock, fruit) and the Visalia Electric freight operation at Alum Rock after 1934 - freight, Rule 1; (6) SP steam passenger service on the Mayfield Cut-off and to Los Gatos - Southern Pacific, not Peninsular. No horsecar years exist: every company here was electric from opening.
not_yet_sourced: End-to-end mileages for the Campbell route, San Jose-Palo Alto, Congress Springs and the Palo Alto locals (only San Jose-Saratoga-Los Gatos has a documented figure).

Every headway is an estimate: hourly for interurbans per Wikipedia/McCaleb and Santa Cruz Trains, 15-20 min for Palo Alto locals per Wikipedia; no dated public timetable was read. A Los Gatos Mail weekly timetable (1908-1912) and McCaleb, Tracks, Tires and Wires (1981) pp.94-97 would settle them.

What ran in 1907-1910 on the Peninsular's new track: chicagorailfan dates San Jose-Cupertino to 1907, Santa Cruz Trains puts a 5 Nov 1907 opening at the Mayfield end, Wikipedia mentions only a 1909 stub on the cut-off. Drawn as San Jose-Cupertino 1907-1910.
Start of Cupertino/Palo Alto-Los Gatos service via Congress Junction: chicagorailfan 4 Jan 1914 (drawn) vs Wikipedia 1910.

End of the via-Saratoga service: 12 Mar 1933 (chicagorailfan; Peninsula Times Tribune via Wikipedia) vs accounts of the final 1934 car running Los Gatos-Saratoga-San Jose (Santa Cruz Trains; Saratoga Historical Foundation, which says March 1934).
Campbell route street order between Hamilton and Campbell Avenue (Union vs Bascom Avenue), and the exact location of the shared SP Almaden-branch track.
Stanford line alignment and campus terminus (Wikipedia's uncited Galvez/Lasuen/Serra description vs Western Railroader's "University and private right of way").
Date the Waverley Street line was extended from Embarcadero Road to Oregon Avenue (not drawn).
Exact location of the Congress Hotel terminus and the 1929-1934 Mayfield terminal.

properties.company: San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban Railway
properties.line: San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban: San Jose – Los Gatos (via Saratoga)
properties.speed_source: Santa Cruz Trains (citing the Journal of Electricity, Power and Gas, July 1905) gives 30 minutes San Jose-Los Gatos via Saratoga, about 15 mi, i.e. ~48 km/h. One contemporary figure for the opening years; later running times not checked, so treat as approximate for 1909-1933.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 15.2 mi against a documented 15 mi (Santa Cruz Trains: 11 mi San Jose-Saratoga, traced 11.18; 4 mi Saratoga-Los Gatos, traced 4.03). No straight-line legs. Street-routed on TODAY'S OpenStreetMap road centrelines (staged street-name Dijkstra over the OSM road graph), following the streets the sources name. Where the interurban ran on private right of way beside a road (San Carlos/Stevens Creek, Saratoga Avenue, Saratoga-Los Gatos Road) it is drawn on the road centreline, a few tens of metres off; these roads have been widened and in places realigned since the 1930s, so this is a LATER ALIGNMENT than the line's own era. Route: Market Street depot loop (Bassett/Market) - South Market - West San Carlos - Stevens Creek Boulevard to Meridian Corners - Saratoga Avenue to Saratoga village - Saratoga-Los Gatos Road - Santa Cruz Avenue to Main Street, Los Gatos. The downtown San Jose one-way pair (Park Avenue westbound) and the Julian/Bassett terminal loop are not drawn; the Los Gatos end stops at Santa Cruz Avenue and Main Street, about 150 m short of the documented Broadway terminal.

segments.note: Opened for regular service 19 March 1904 (Santa Cruz Trains; chicagorailfan route table; Wikipedia service table) - electric from the start, so no horsecar years. O. A. Hale, widely understood to be acting for the Southern Pacific, took control of the company on 9 April 1904, but the line went on running under the San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban name until it was consolidated into the Peninsular Railway on 30 June 1909; the feature is split there (Rule 4). Santa Cruz Trains notes the old name kept appearing on newspaper timetables until March 1912 - a holdover, not a different operator. Headway: Wikipedia's service table (citing McCaleb 1981) and Santa Cruz Trains both give hourly service each way; treated as an ESTIMATE for the whole span, not a count from a dated timetable. The 1905 Journal of Electricity description has cars leaving San Jose on the hour for Saratoga first and on the half hour for Campbell first, i.e. hourly each way round the loop.
sources: Segment-level: opening date and 1909 consolidation from Santa Cruz Trains (San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban) and the chicagorailfan route table; headway is an estimate.

Southern Pacific owned the Peninsular, but it ran its trains under its own name, timetables and red livery until abandonment, so it keeps its own colour rather than SP's (judgment recorded in metadata). properties.line: San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban: San Jose – Los Gatos (via Campbell)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE. No running time found for the Campbell route; set below the via-Saratoga figure because of the street running and the shared-track stops at the SP Almaden branch junctions (up to ten minutes, Santa Cruz Trains).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 12.5 mi; no documented end-to-end mileage found. No straight-line legs; 0.23 mi of the route runs on connector roads rather than the named streets. Street-routed on TODAY'S OpenStreetMap road centrelines (staged street-name Dijkstra over the OSM road graph), following the streets the sources name. Where the interurban ran on private right of way beside a road (San Carlos/Stevens Creek, Saratoga Avenue, Saratoga-Los Gatos Road) it is drawn on the road centreline, a few tens of metres off; these roads have been widened and in places realigned since the 1930s, so this is a LATER ALIGNMENT than the line's own era. Street order is from Santa Cruz Trains and Wikipedia: Market - West San Carlos - Bird Avenue - Coe - Lincoln - Willow - Meridian - Hamilton - Bascom - Campbell Avenue (SOURCE CONFLICT: Santa Cruz Trains has the line using Union Avenue between Hamilton and Campbell Avenue, Wikipedia/McCaleb has Bascom Avenue; Bascom is drawn). Campbell Avenue to Camden Avenue is drawn on the ex-SP Vasona line (OSM "Vasona Industrial Lead") because the interurban ran on its own track beside the SP there; Camden Avenue east is today's Camden Avenue/San Tomas Expressway (one 50 m snap between two disconnected Camden Avenue ways); then Bascom Avenue - Los Gatos Boulevard - Main Street, Los Gatos. segments.note: Cars ran Los Gatos-Campbell from 24 November 1904 (Santa Cruz Trains; the chicagorailfan table dates the route 26 November 1904), and the Campbell-San Jose link was completed over several months after the San Jose city council granted the downtown route on 23 January 1905, so the through route is drawn from 1905. SOURCE CONFLICT: Wikipedia's service table (McCaleb 1981) dates the San Jose-Campbell-Los Gatos service from 1907 and says the Peninsular built it; Santa Cruz Trains' account (citing the July 1905 Journal of Electricity, which mapped and described the completed loop) is the more specific and is followed. Run as part of the San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban until the 30 June 1909 consolidation. Headway: Wikipedia's service table (citing McCaleb 1981) and Santa Cruz Trains both give hourly service each way; treated as an ESTIMATE for the whole span, not a count from a dated timetable.
sources: Segment-level: November 1904 / 1905 openings from Santa Cruz Trains and the chicagorailfan table; conflicting 1907 date from Wikipedia recorded; headway is an estimate.

properties.company: San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban Railway
properties.line: San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban: Saratoga – Congress Springs
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE; short, steep resort branch with irregular service. No timetable found.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 1.45 mi; no documented mileage found. Street-routed on today's Big Basin Way / State Route 9 from Saratoga village. The branch ended at the Congress Hotel at Congress Springs; the drawn line stops on SR 9 about 640 m (0.4 mi) short of the mapped Congress Springs spring because the branch's last stretch off the highway is not located - NOT extended by a straight line. Today's highway alignment, not the branch's own grade (Santa Cruz Trains mentions several small bridges on the branch).

segments.note: Opened 10 July 1904 (Santa Cruz Trains; Wikipedia). SOURCE CONFLICT: the chicagorailfan table gives 26 November 1904. Either way 1904. A picnic/resort branch to the Congress Hotel; Wikipedia calls the service "irregular", so the 120-minute headway is a placeholder ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1904 opening from Santa Cruz Trains, Wikipedia and the chicagorailfan table (which disagree on the day); headway is a placeholder estimate.

segments.note: The chicagorailfan route table dates Peninsular San Jose-Cupertino service from 1907 (no day given), and Santa Cruz Trains says the Peninsular Railroad's first new line opened 5 November 1907 - it reads that as the Mayfield end, but the cut-off itself only opened on 19 April 1908 and through Palo Alto cars began 5 March 1910, so the 1907 opening is taken to be the Stevens Creek line to Cupertino. This was the Peninsular RAILROAD (incorporated by O. A. Hale on 21 December 1905), run separately from the San Jose and Los Gatos Interurban until both were consolidated as the Peninsular Railway on 30 June 1909; the 1905 and 1909 companies are treated as one company here (same SP-controlled corporation, reincorporated). Ends in 1910 when the service became the through San Jose-Palo Alto line (separate feature). SOURCE CONFLICT: Wikipedia says only "stub service along the Mayfield cut-off operated in 1909". Headway ESTIMATE.

properties.line: Peninsular Railway: San Jose – Palo Alto (via Los Altos)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE. Hourly cars, single track with passing sidings on the cut-off (double track on Stevens Creek); no end-to-end running time found.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 20.72 mi; no documented end-to-end mileage found (pieces: San Jose-Monta Vista 10.02 mi street-routed, Monta Vista-El Camino Real 8.56 mi on the Mayfield Cut-off, El Camino Real-Palo Alto depot 2.12 mi street-routed on El Camino Real, an APPROXIMATION of the Peninsular's Mayfield-Palo Alto track). No straight-line legs. Street-routed on TODAY'S OpenStreetMap road centrelines (staged street-name Dijkstra over the OSM road graph), following the streets the sources name. Where the interurban ran on private right of way beside a road (San Carlos/Stevens Creek, Saratoga Avenue, Saratoga-Los Gatos Road) it is drawn on the road centreline, a few tens of metres off; these roads have been widened and in places realigned since the 1930s, so this is a LATER ALIGNMENT than the line's own era. Mayfield Cut-off section traced from OpenHistoricalMap relation 2749538 "Los Altos Branch" (CC0; ways 198540837, 199596214, 199596213, 198748393; geometry only, OHM dates not used). That is the Southern Pacific branch line; the Peninsular's own electrified track ran on the same right of way beside it (Santa Cruz Trains; Wikipedia Mayfield Cutoff), so the drawn line is the SP track a few metres from the interurban track. Peninsular cars on this section were Peninsular service on Peninsular-electrified track within an SP-owned right of way. The Stevens Creek line is drawn west to where Stevens Creek Boulevard crosses the cut-off at Monta Vista, the junction the sources describe.

segments.note: Through electric service San Jose-Palo Alto began 5 March 1910 (Hilton & Due 2000 p.404 via Wikipedia; chicagorailfan table; Western Railroader Aug 1951 p.7). Peninsular cars ran over the SP Mayfield Cut-off right of way on their own electrified track between Monta Vista and Mayfield; once they ran, SP's steam trains on the cut-off dropped their intermediate stops (Saratoga Historical Foundation). Palo Alto made the Peninsular give up its Mayfield-Palo Alto track for the widening of El Camino Real; service was cut back to Mayfield on 21 October 1929 (Western Railroader; chicagorailfan). Hourly (Wikipedia; Santa Cruz Trains) - ESTIMATE across the whole span.
sources: Segment-level: 5 March 1910 start and 21 October 1929 cut-back from Hilton & Due (via Wikipedia), the Western Railroader August 1951 date list and the chicagorailfan table; headway is an estimate.

properties.line: Santa Clara Interurban: University Avenue (Palo Alto)
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 1.82 mi, University Avenue from the SP depot to the San Francisquito Creek bridge; no documented mileage. Street-routed on today's OpenStreetMap road centrelines in Palo Alto. Drawn to the creek; early cars briefly ran a few hundred feet beyond it (Western Railroader) - not drawn.

segments.note: Palo Alto's street railway opened 15 November 1906 under the Santa Clara Interurban Railroad (Western Railroader Aug 1951, quoting the Palo Alto Times; chicagorailfan table). Electric from opening (the original six cars were trolleys, later rebuilt for one-man operation). Acquired by the Peninsular Railway 30 June 1909 - split there (Rule 4). Headway 15-20 min per Wikipedia's table; ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 15 November 1906 opening and 30 June 1909 acquisition from the Western Railroader August 1951 and the chicagorailfan table; headway from Wikipedia's table, an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 1.82 mi, University Avenue from the SP depot to the San Francisquito Creek bridge; no documented mileage. Street-routed on today's OpenStreetMap road centrelines in Palo Alto. Many runs turned at Pope Street (Western Railroader) - the full creek run is drawn.

segments.note: Peninsular Railway from 30 June 1909. Replaced by buses in July 1925 (chicagorailfan: 20 July 1925; Wikipedia: last day 19 July 1925). Cut back from beyond the creek to the near side of the bridge after a dispute with the county over bridge maintenance (Western Railroader). Headway 15-20 min per Wikipedia - ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1909 acquisition and July 1925 end from the Western Railroader August 1951, the chicagorailfan table and Wikipedia; headway an estimate.

properties.line: Santa Clara Interurban: Waverley Street (Palo Alto)
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 1.07 mi: Waverley Street from Embarcadero Road to University Avenue, then University Avenue to the SP depot; no documented mileage. Street-routed on today's OpenStreetMap road centrelines in Palo Alto. The line was later extended south from Embarcadero Road to Oregon Avenue (Western Railroader), date unknown - NOT drawn.

segments.note: The chicagorailfan table dates the Waverley Street line, like University Avenue, from the 15 November 1906 opening under the Santa Clara Interurban (Wikipedia's table leaves its start blank). Acquired by the Peninsular 30 June 1909. Headway ESTIMATE (15-20 min per Wikipedia).
sources: Segment-level: 1906 start from the chicagorailfan table; 1909 acquisition from the Western Railroader August 1951; headway an estimate.

segments.note: Peninsular Railway from 30 June 1909 until replaced by buses in September 1925 (Wikipedia: 27 September 1925, citing the Palo Alto Times of 24 September 1925; chicagorailfan: 28 September 1925). Headway ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1909 acquisition and September 1925 end from Wikipedia (Palo Alto Times), the chicagorailfan table and the Western Railroader; headway an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 1.37 mi; no documented mileage. APPROXIMATED on today's streets: SP depot - El Camino Real - Galvez Street (past the stadium) - Lasuen Street, ending near the Main Quad, following Wikipedia's uncited description (leased track along Galvez, Lasuen Street, Serra Mall to the Palm Drive Oval). SOURCE CONFLICT: the Western Railroader (1951) says the line ran "on University and private right of way to Stanford" and that its campus terminus moved over the years (near the library, later the corporation yard). The campus end of the drawn line is therefore uncertain by a few hundred metres.

segments.note: Opened 6 October 1909 (Wikipedia; the Western Railroader date list gives 1909). SOURCE CONFLICT: the chicagorailfan table gives 5 March 1910, the day through San Jose cars began. Last car 20 October 1929, abandoned 21 October 1929 with the Mayfield-Palo Alto interurban track (Wikipedia citing the Palo Alto Times of 21 October 1929; Western Railroader). After the downtown lines closed in 1925 it ran depot-campus only. Heavy football-day traffic to the stadium (Saratoga Historical Foundation). Headway is a placeholder ESTIMATE - no source gives one.
sources: Segment-level: 6 October 1909 start (Wikipedia, Western Railroader) and 21 October 1929 end (Wikipedia/Palo Alto Times, Western Railroader, chicagorailfan); headway is a placeholder estimate.
